english: For, if ordinary mind itself is realized, attachment and hatred are absent; ethical discipline also abandons them, and that too depends on the Ground, the nature of phenomena. Clear realization of Mahamudra must depend on the ground of ethical discipline. They share the function of abandoning the three poisons and accomplishing temporary and ultimate qualities, and they are one with emptiness, the actual condition as it is.[^N-C-034]

notes.problem: གཞི appears both as the technical Ground and as the supporting ground of ethical discipline. The glossary has intentional internal capitalization not otherwise explained.
notes.treatment: Keep the Ground for the technical ground/path/result usage, lower-case ground where ordinary support is meant; preserve the lexical term.
notes.uncertainty: The contextual and capitalization distinction is provisional.
notes.review_action: Review presentation once for this range; no change to the glossary.

english: Likewise:

If there were no buddha element,
There would be no disenchantment with suffering,
No desire for nirvāṇa,
And no aspiration to seek it.
The noble master said:

Ethical discipline is said to be the supporting ground of all qualities,
As earth is for the moving and the unmoving.
And:

For ordinary people, those born from the [Buddha’s] speech,
Those whose character is fixed on solitary awakening,
And the children of the victorious ones, there is no cause
Of definite goodness and higher rebirth other than ethical discipline.[^N-C-035]

notes.problem: The possessor of speech is not explicit in this compound.
notes.treatment: Supply [Buddha’s] for the conventional epithet of hearers.
notes.uncertainty: The doctrinal referent is likely; the source remains abbreviated.
notes.review_action: Review the compound together with the four classes listed.

english: And:
Through ethical discipline, those who desire peace become noble.
And the King of Deep Absorption says:

By cultivating emptiness, this king of deep absorption,
One stands at the summit of pure ethical discipline.
Having rested in equipoise in phenomena’s emptiness of intrinsic nature,
The childish, intent on touching fire, do not know [this].[^N-C-036]

notes.problem: The subject changes awkwardly between the equipoise clause and the childish touching fire; a defect in the quoted text is possible.
notes.treatment: Retain the sequence and fire image; supply only [this] as the implicit object of not knowing.
notes.uncertainty: The attachment is unresolved and this verse is not a settled reading.
notes.review_action: Check all four lines of the quotation in a witness.

english: So it is said. In brief, although both are free of afflictions, they do not interrupt wholesome Dharma activity. Though there is no fear of falling into bad destinies, they are one in [avoiding] even subtle wrongdoing.[^N-C-037]

notes.problem: The phrase literally connects subtle wrongdoing with being one, but lacks an explicit verb of avoidance. The later parallel U03753 supplies such a verb.
notes.treatment: Supply [avoiding] visibly from the parallel argument; retain the unity of Mahamudra and discipline.
notes.uncertainty: This is a contextual reconstruction, not an authenticated reading.
notes.review_action: Compare U03615 with U03750–U03753 and a physical witness.

english: Vajra statement. Some say, “Mahamudra is like space, so it cannot be assigned to virtue or nonvirtue; it is emptiness without faults or qualities.” Here, Mahamudra abides as the very character of all qualities throughout the Ground, path, and result. At the time of the Ground, disenchantment with suffering and the arising of desire and aspiration for nirvāṇa are the power of the element. The Supreme Continuum says:

If there were no buddha element,
There would be no disenchantment with suffering,
No aspiration for nirvāṇa,
And no wish to seek it.

So it is said. The lama’s pointing out that very Ground and one’s becoming familiar with it is called the path. Through its power, whatever roots of virtue one undertakes become immeasurable. The Mother says:
“Those who wish to pervade all world systems with a single flower or a single parasol should train in the perfection of discerning knowing.”

So it is said. At the time of the result, the Dharma embodiment, together with its qualities and deeds, arises without interruption; thus it abides as the very character of qualities. In brief, throughout the Ground, path, and result, it abides without removing faults or adding qualities. The Supreme Continuum says:

There is nothing here to remove,
And not the slightest thing to add.
Look authentically at the authentic;
Seeing authentically, one is fully liberated.
So it is said.
[1] Vajra statement. Some say that qualities do not arise from equipoise but from post-cultivation attainment, citing Lord Atiśa:

If ordinary mind is stable in equipoise,
Do not give priority to virtue of body and speech.

They also say that equipoise is like space. Further, there is the claim here that both virtue and nonvirtue obscure Mahamudra itself because they are formations, citing the Root [Verses on] Discerning Knowing:[^N-C-038]

notes.problem: The source uses འདིར while still presenting a claim later explicitly rejected at U03656.
notes.treatment: Keep here but identify the claim as reported rather than the author’s conclusion.
notes.uncertainty: The discourse boundary may reflect defective punctuation or wording.

english: The root of saṃsāra is formations.

They say this is like white and black clouds: there is no difference in their obscuring the sun. Here, however, the essence of virtue cannot obscure Mahamudra in the Ground, path, or result. Like a lake and its waves, methods such as the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening arise from it itself and make its essence grow ever greater. Through going for refuge and so forth, at buddhahood there arises nothing but the wheel of the Jewels.
For every virtue done at the Ground and on the path ultimately, at buddhahood, brings inconceivable enlightened activity into uninterrupted engagement with the realms of beings.

It is held that all qualities arise during equipoise. On attaining the path of seeing there are twelve sets of one hundred qualities; on the second ground, twelve sets of one thousand; on the fourth, twelve sets of one hundred koṭis; on the fifth, twelve sets of one thousand koṭis; on the sixth, twelve sets of one hundred thousand koṭis; on the seventh, twelve sets of one hundred thousand khrak-khrik; on the eighth, twelve times the number of particles in one hundred thousand great thousandfold world systems; and on the ninth, twelve times the number of particles in ten hundred thousand great thousandfold world systems.[^N-C-039]

notes.problem: The enumeration omits the third ground. Large-number names vary by system and the particle counts must not be reduced to twelve particles.
notes.treatment: Preserve the stated factorized quantities; retain koṭi and khrak-khrik without decimal conversion. Translate སྟོང་ཆེན contextually as great thousandfold world system.
notes.uncertainty: The value of khrak-khrik and the omitted third-ground quantity remain unverified.
notes.review_action: Check the numerical tradition and the missing third-ground entry; do not silently insert it.

english: On the tenth ground, [the qualities number] the particles of the inexpressible: seeing the faces of buddhas and knowing their blessings; going to their fields; entering and emerging from deep absorption; shaking fields; making fields appear; opening Dharma gateways; maturing beings; abiding for aeons; directing the gaze of primordial knowing to former abodes; displaying bodies; and displaying a surrounding retinue of “scripture and awareness.”[^N-C-040]

notes.problem: The tenth-ground quantity lacks an explicit counted cosmic unit; the last item’s ལུང་རིག is anomalous in a list of retinues. U03683 contains repeated tshegs.
notes.treatment: Supply the quantitative link in brackets, retain the particle expression, and quote scripture and awareness as unresolved wording rather than inventing a retinue.
notes.uncertainty: A defective final item is probable; the correct reading is unknown.
notes.review_action: Collate the complete twelve-quality list and tenth-ground quantity.

english: As equipoise grows, qualities also increase. The inconceivable qualities at the culmination of the ten grounds, and the enlightened activity that matures and liberates beings after buddhahood, all arise from equipoise. Lord Phakdru said:

The qualities of bodhisattvas on the ten grounds
Are their abiding in the unborn.

So it is said. Were it otherwise, qualities ought to arise in lower ordinary beings but not in buddhas, because ordinary beings have only subsequent knowing, whereas buddhas never lack equipoise. This is refuted by the statement that the difference between the qualities of buddhas and tenth-ground bodhisattvas is like that between an ocean and the water in a cow’s hoofprint.[^N-C-041]

notes.problem: The reference is blank. རྗེ་ཤེས appears to stand for subsequent knowing, contrasted with equipoise; the source lacks the usual final letter of རྗེས.
notes.treatment: Translate subsequent knowing provisionally, retaining the original source.
notes.uncertainty: The textual form and its relation to post-cultivation attainment need review.
notes.review_action: Check U03698 against U03714 and a witness.

english: Vajra statement. Some say, “If one realizes Dharma embodiment Mahamudra, all qualities arise even without accomplishing their causes.” Here, all qualities cannot arise without accomplishing their causes, for otherwise qualities would arise even in someone who had not gathered the two accumulations. Accordingly, the Heap of Jewels says:

Through the causes and conditions of inconceivable
Virtuous karma on the grounds,
By completely abandoning bewilderment,
Various rays of light are accomplished.[^N-C-042]

notes.problem: The attachment of grounds to inconceivable virtuous karma is compressed, and ས་ནི might instead be an independent topic.
notes.treatment: Read on the grounds provisionally while preserving the causal and instrumental sequence.
notes.uncertainty: The exact topic relation remains uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check the full verse in the cited sūtra.

english: Countless such statements are taught. Qualities arising in equipoise and not arising without accomplishing their causes are not contradictory: the causes are accomplished without separation from that state, so this does not become subsequent knowing. For the Condensed [Perfection] says, “There is no conceited ordinary mind thinking, ‘I am in equipoise,’ or ‘I have arisen.’”

Addendum. Some say that the qualities of results of separation do not require causes. Here, all results of separation have causes, because a result without a cause is impossible in the actual condition. Thus, in the Sūtra of the Questions of the Girl Ratna:[^N-C-043]

notes.problem: This technical result category is absent from the active glossary, as is the source label ལྷན༽༽.
notes.treatment: Use result of separation provisionally; visibly render the label Addendum throughout this range.
notes.uncertainty: The intended scholastic category should be confirmed.
notes.review_action: Review the whole-expression term and retain all source labels.

english: “Girl, when practicing bodhisattva activity, one possesses the power of teaching that this Lesser Vehicle is impossible and has no occasion [to occur]. At buddhahood one will attain the power of knowing what is possible and impossible.” Such things are said.[^N-C-044]

notes.problem: The precise impossibility concerning the Lesser Vehicle is not specified, and the clause may be incomplete.
notes.treatment: Retain the stated vehicle and impossibility; bracket the minimal verbal supply rather than inventing a fall or exclusion.
notes.uncertainty: The quotation’s intended scope is unresolved.
notes.review_action: Check the complete passage in the Sūtra of the Questions of the Girl Ratna.

english: Vajra statement. Some say, “Since all phenomena are no other than one’s own ordinary mind, when its nature of phenomena is realized through the path, all the diverse appearances of virtue, nonvirtue, karma, results, and so on are realized as emptiness without appearance. There is no causal dependent arising, just as in space.”

Here, when emptiness is realized, causal dependent arising itself occurs inseparably from it, without obstruction, like an illusory appearance. Thus emptiness does not block cause and result. For example, when a rainbow arising in space appears inseparably from that space, space does not block the rainbow. Accordingly, the King of Deep Absorption says:

Though one knows that in the nature of phenomena there is no karmic ripening,
Virtuous and nonvirtuous karma does not go to waste.
That vehicle of solitary victors, abiding in peace,
Follows the word of the hearers’ liberation.[^N-C-045]

notes.problem: The latter two lines have an unclear subject and logical relation to the preceding karmic statement.
notes.treatment: Retain the visible vehicle, hearers, liberation, and word relationships without importing a familiar alternate quotation.
notes.uncertainty: The text may be incomplete or defective.

english: The Sūtra of the Questions of Jönpa says:

Blessed One, skilled in dependence on causes,
Never possessing views of the two extremes,
You teach precisely the ripened results of karma.
Homage to you, free from the darkness of views.
So it is said. The Jetsün gave Gampopa this Dharma instruction at his departure:

Though you have no hope for buddhahood above,
Do not interrupt wholesome Dharma activity.
Though you have no fear of bad destinies below,
Shun even the subtlest wrongdoing.
So he said, and more.

If one thinks this contradictory, it is not. The King of Deep Absorption speaks of “the king of deep absorption in the evenness of all phenomena, extensively elaborated.” Evenness is emptiness; extensive elaboration is the elaboration of causal dependent arising. These two are taught as noncontradictory. Likewise:

For whom emptiness is tenable,
Everything is tenable.
And:

There is no phenomenon whatsoever
Apart from dependent arising.
Therefore, [something] that is not emptiness—[quotation breaks off].[^N-C-046]

notes.problem: The quotation stops at a genitive phrase before its conclusion.
notes.treatment: Translate the available clause and mark the break explicitly; do not restore the familiar missing line.
notes.uncertainty: The absence is in the fixed transcript, not proof of omission in a physical witness.
notes.review_action: Collate the quotation and preserve the original partial reading.

english: So it is said. Therefore, even when ultimate omniscience is attained, there is emergence or occurrence from the state free from conceptual elaborations without abandoning the fine distinctions of cause and result.
